text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) said the recent inflow of hard currency from abroad was not big enough to fix the crown at devaluation levels.

- The NBS said domestic banks shortened their forex positions by some $150 million to fulfil minimum reserves requirement in mid-January. But the central bank said banks will not be able to continue with these moves for longer periods as they have to meet required forex positions.

- Jacobs Suchard Figaro a.s., controlled by the U.S.-based Philip Morris Cos Inc, will hold an extraordinary shareholders meeting following accusations that the majority owner channels out profits, damaging the rights of minority shareholders.
- Slovakia's largest insurer, state-owned Slovenska Poistovna s.p., expects to post net profit of around 300 million crowns in 1996.
NARODNA OBRODA - Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar is expected to visit Japan this year.

- Defence Minister Jan Sitek on Wednesday met with NATO General Secretary Javier Solana. Sitek repeatedly said that intergration to the alliance remains one of Slovakia's top foreign policy priorities.

- Parlaimentary Chairman Ivan Gasparovic has excluded a proposal to indefinitely postpone privatisation of four largest financial institutions from the agenda of the next session, starting February 4. The opposition Party of Democratic Left (SDL) said it would propose this legislative change again at the beginning of the session.
- The exchange of privatisation bonds for shares from the portfolio of the National Property Fund is likely to start in the second half of February.

SLOVENSKA REPUBLIKA - Austrian Vice-chancellor and Foreign Minister Wolfgang Schuessel arrives on Thursday for a one-day visit to Slovakia. Schuessel will meet his counterpart Pavol Hamzik, President Michal Kovac and Prime Minister Meciar.
